# s390 — The post-merge hook says when slicer is missing, and a test runs its install command

**Findings:** s384 relay report 2026-10-22, later notes 1 and 3: when slicer is not on PATH the hook prints only "run slicer check", and no test runs the printed install command · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-11-09** — Verified: the post-merge hook printed by setup-git --hook now tests shell status 127 before the other cases and prints 'slicer: slicer was not found on PATH; install it or add it to PATH, then run slicer check.' on stderr, exits 0 and renders nothing (src/slicer/cli_setup.py). Two tests in PostMergeHookTests: SlicerNotOnPath runs the printed hook through sh with a PATH that has no slicer; HookInstall runs the printed install command in a fixture git repo, with and without core.hooksPath, and checks an executable file holding the hook text. The first was red before the change; the second covers existing behaviour and was mutation-checked instead. docs/commands.md and CHANGELOG.md updated. Full suite 3322 tests, 0 failed, 1 skipped; slicer check exits 0.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** installing the hook for the person, the roadmap-only detection, and a change to the merge driver.

## Why

`_post_merge_hook` in `src/slicer/cli_setup.py` captures `slicer check --json` and, for any status other than the roadmap-only case, prints "merge check needs attention; run slicer check." When `slicer` is not on PATH the shell status is 127, so the person is told to run a command that is the very thing missing. The s384 tests assert the install command's text but none runs it, so a quoting mistake in the `git rev-parse --git-path` form would pass the suite.

## Files

- `src/slicer/cli_setup.py` (`_post_merge_hook`).
- `tests/test_cli.py`, `PostMergeHookTests`, next to the s384 post-merge hook tests.
- `docs/commands.md` (the post-merge hook paragraph under `setup-git`) and `CHANGELOG.md` under Changed.

## Failing tests

- `test_PostMergeHook_SlicerNotOnPath_NamesTheMissingCommand`: run the printed hook with a PATH that has no `slicer`; it prints a line that says slicer was not found, exits 0 and renders nothing.
- `test_SetupGit_HookInstall_CommandInstallsExecutableHook`: in a fixture git repo, run the printed install command through `sh`; `git rev-parse --git-path hooks/post-merge` names an executable file with the hook text, and a `core.hooksPath` setting is honoured.

## Implement

1. Write the tests; watch them go red.
2. In the hook, test for status 127 before the other cases and print a line that says slicer was not found on PATH. The status stays 0.
3. Update the docs and CHANGELOG if they describe the hook text.
4. Mutation-check each new test.
